approach.method_basis: The Parent evolves molecular graphs from real accepted scores. It selects breeding parents across high-scoring population quantiles, applies connected-fragment crossover and ordinary successive atom and bond edits, and fills a fresh surplus pool after graph validation and canonical duplicate rejection. Direct aromatic carbon/nitrogen exchange is disabled. A Gaussian process uses the complete task-local accepted archive, folded integer Morgan environment counts and fixed dot-product Tanimoto covariance. Correlated sampled functions select distinct offspring for evaluation; accepted scores then update the archive and a bounded greedy population.
approach.novelty: Substitute one fixed Matérn-3/2 covariance on normalized count composition for the current Tanimoto law. Euclidean distance between unit-length count rows changes similarity and roughness while retaining the same extracted fingerprints and all other search operations. This differs from siblings that unfolded the count coordinates, added an atom-pair channel, replaced the model by trees or removed predictive selection. Normalization deliberately loses overall count scale and aliases proportional count rows; these are risks of this single recipe, not separately identified effects. The hypothesis is that its changed geometry improves prospective ordering and delivery of useful scored offspring, which may improve the complete endpoint mean.

hypothesis: Replace dot-product count Tanimoto covariance with fixed Matérn-3/2 covariance on L2-normalized unchanged folded Morgan count rows: z(x)=x/||x||2 for nonzero x and z(0)=0; r=||z(x)-z(y)||2; K(x,y)=(1+sqrt(3)*r)*exp(-sqrt(3)*r), with lengthscale one and unit amplitude.

Average best-generating-parent score fell from 0.470456 to 0.416185, and offspring score from 0.385256 to 0.338080: beating weaker sources more often is not independent evidence of stronger exploration. No evidence identifies that chemistry as a mediated consequence of covariance geometry. End this exact exposed complete law under the registered rule. molecular.headline: Ring-rich aromatic families persist, with reactive N/O-halogen bonds, occasional oligomer growth and unspecified stereochemistry
molecular.overall_character: Complete Child evaluation and complete matched Parent pairing are explicitly true in context.comparison; all fifteen Child and fifteen published Parent trajectory paths and their task logs were present and read. All five digest objectives are covered, with no tasks_without_trajectories. Each objective has 900 trajectory rows including 870 optimizer proposals. The parent-only molecules used for chemistry comparisons are not included in cited_smiles because the trusted allowlist contains Child trajectories only. Signed endpoint evidence for every task/seed appears below, including all losses. The Child and Parent are separate three-seed panels sharing one baseline; chemical associations and exact generating provenance do not identify Matérn mediation, activation, independent replication, or component-specific effects. Chemistry spans indole amides, linked azaaromatic heterocycles, small/medium-ring aryl amines, dense dicarbonyl systems and fluorinated imino/dione families. Ring and aromaticity are rich, consistent with digest ring-closure-string incidences 0.9874 to 0.9989 and aromatic-string incidences 0.9839 to 0.9977. These incidences are SMILES-text molecule indicators, not perceived ring counts. Synthetic plausibility is questionable and overall drug-likeness weak because reactive heteroatom-halogen bonds, unresolved tautomer/stability questions, dense topology and occasional large oligomers accompany familiar medicinal groups. Diversity is moderate across seeds and objectives but narrower within leading families; no independent core diversity claim follows from distinct strings. Heavy-atom sizes and perceived rings mentioned in this report come from RDKit parsing the actual cited trajectory molecules in the read-only support audit, never oracle evaluation. No synthesis, stability, affinity or conformational feasibility measurement is available. Initial rows are fixed starting observations; best retained endpoints, last proposals and digest final_molecules are distinguished: the digest final excerpt is late seed-2 proposals, not all three final retained leaders. Actual generating-parent/emission/accepted joins are recorded for every leader below and fully retained in .slots/round-0026-slot-1/molecular_audit.json. Incumbent-improvement flags are logged during sequential processing of each accepted batch and must not be mistaken for the preregistered batch pre-feedback incumbent statistic. method_name: Mol GA: rank-selected de novo graph evolution
method_thesis: Anchor the root in Mol GA: maintain a population of oracle-evaluated molecular graphs, sample breeding parents across high-ranked quantiles, generate new offspring through graph crossover and atom/bond mutations, and update survivors greedily after each observation. These are the proposal and selection mechanisms described by [Tripp and Hernández-Lobato (2023)](https://arxiv.org/html/2310.09267v1). Start from the supplied initial observations and incorporate newly evaluated offspring immediately, following the evaluator's announced batching. Repeated graph edits and recombination create an evolving search space; no corpus ranking, stored molecule library, pretrained model, or fixed candidate enumeration is needed. The causal hypothesis is that direct selection on task-local scores concentrates successive structural changes around improving molecules quickly enough to raise the final best observed score. The published evidence concerns a larger-budget AUC-Top-10 setting, so its transfer to this benchmark's final Top-1 objective remains a hypothesis.

finding_summary.insights: The failure is informative because the new predictor had real allocation exposure, complete accepted feedback and intact numerical controls: an inactive implementation or unseen changed choices cannot explain the negative endpoint result. More parent-beating offspring and incumbent events did not translate into better final best molecules. Average best-generating-parent score fell from 0.470456 to 0.416185, and offspring score from 0.385256 to 0.338080: beating weaker sources more often is not independent evidence of stronger exploration. The original predictor also ranks the very same scored Child selections better, narrowing the predictive hypothesis without requiring unscored pool labels. Local event counts and selected-stream errors cannot stand in for the benchmark objective. Normalizing count rows deliberately loses overall count scale and introduces proportional-coordinate aliases by construction, although no proportional-only pairs or zero rows were naturally exposed in this panel; those effects belong to the complete tested covariance recipe and were not separately randomized or attributed. Productive-event reuse, later conditioning and descendant cores remain conditional associations with overlapping ancestry and censored final-batch sources. The chemistry assessment also shows familiar useful carbonyl/aromatic and amine frameworks alongside reactive heteroatom-halogen arrangements, unresolved stereochemistry and occasional large elaborations; compact leaders and useful deletions show that blanket growth, fluorination or fragmentation rules are not justified. No evidence identifies that chemistry as a mediated consequence of covariance geometry. End this exact exposed complete law under the registered rule. A future materially different law needs a sourced distinguishing hypothesis; transferable kernel-family benefit and independent plausible descendant coverage remain open.

finding_summary.headline: Changed allocations and more local gains, but mean Top-1 falls by 0.02751
finding_summary.insights: The failure is informative because the new predictor had real allocation exposure, complete accepted feedback and intact numerical controls: an inactive implementation or unseen changed choices cannot explain the negative endpoint result. More parent-beating offspring and incumbent events did not translate into better final best molecules. Average best-generating-parent score fell from 0.470456 to 0.416185, and offspring score from 0.385256 to 0.338080: beating weaker sources more often is not independent evidence of stronger exploration. The original predictor also ranks the very same scored Child selections better, narrowing the predictive hypothesis without requiring unscored pool labels. Local event counts and selected-stream errors cannot stand in for the benchmark objective. Normalizing count rows deliberately loses overall count scale and introduces proportional-coordinate aliases by construction, although no proportional-only pairs or zero rows were naturally exposed in this panel; those effects belong to the complete tested covariance recipe and were not separately randomized or attributed. Productive-event reuse, later conditioning and descendant cores remain conditional associations with overlapping ancestry and censored final-batch sources. The chemistry assessment also shows familiar useful carbonyl/aromatic and amine frameworks alongside reactive heteroatom-halogen arrangements, unresolved stereochemistry and occasional large elaborations; compact leaders and useful deletions show that blanket growth, fluorination or fragmentation rules are not justified. No evidence identifies that chemistry as a mediated consequence of covariance geometry. End this exact exposed complete law under the registered rule. A future materially different law needs a sourced distinguishing hypothesis; transferable kernel-family benefit and independent plausible descendant coverage remain open.
finding_summary.results: The replacement changed 434 of 435 accepted candidate sets and 435 selection orders when compared with the original predictor on exactly the same pools, earlier observations and random draws. All 4,350 Child offspring reached real feedback with their original pre-label predictions; no formal numerical fallback or rejection occurred. On those actual Child selections, unequal-label pair-order accuracy was 0.646947, versus 0.731356 for passive original predictions; average defined within-batch Spearman was 0.380506, versus 0.579077. Raw-unit selected-stream MSE was 0.012160, versus 0.007080 for the passive original and 0.032088 for the archive mean. The actual Parent stream had pair accuracy 0.711063, Spearman 0.532208 and MSE 0.012718; those adaptive streams differ after the first batch. Strict best-generating-parent beats increased from 629 to 682, and sequential incumbent advances from 258 to 269. Batch-frozen incumbent beats were 373 versus 346. Despite those local events, mean final Top-1 fell from 0.595669649733 to 0.568161409345, a signed change of -0.027508240389. Seed macro changes were -0.062538302981, +0.001846540890, -0.021832959074; 4 of 15 task/seed endpoints improved. Population seed dispersion was 0.007592488960 versus 0.026592870628. The complete +0.002 gain criterion failed.

molecular_assessment.headline: Ring-rich aromatic families persist, with reactive N/O-halogen bonds, occasional oligomer growth and unspecified stereochemistry
molecular_assessment.overall_character: Complete Child evaluation and complete matched Parent pairing are explicitly true in context.comparison; all fifteen Child and fifteen published Parent trajectory paths and their task logs were present and read. All five digest objectives are covered, with no tasks_without_trajectories. Each objective has 900 trajectory rows including 870 optimizer proposals. The parent-only molecules used for chemistry comparisons are not included in cited_smiles because the trusted allowlist contains Child trajectories only. Signed endpoint evidence for every task/seed appears below, including all losses. The Child and Parent are separate three-seed panels sharing one baseline; chemical associations and exact generating provenance do not identify Matérn mediation, activation, independent replication, or component-specific effects. Chemistry spans indole amides, linked azaaromatic heterocycles, small/medium-ring aryl amines, dense dicarbonyl systems and fluorinated imino/dione families. Ring and aromaticity are rich, consistent with digest ring-closure-string incidences 0.9874 to 0.9989 and aromatic-string incidences 0.9839 to 0.9977. These incidences are SMILES-text molecule indicators, not perceived ring counts. Synthetic plausibility is questionable and overall drug-likeness weak because reactive heteroatom-halogen bonds, unresolved tautomer/stability questions, dense topology and occasional large oligomers accompany familiar medicinal groups. Diversity is moderate across seeds and objectives but narrower within leading families; no independent core diversity claim follows from distinct strings. Heavy-atom sizes and perceived rings mentioned in this report come from RDKit parsing the actual cited trajectory molecules in the read-only support audit, never oracle evaluation. No synthesis, stability, affinity or conformational feasibility measurement is available. Initial rows are fixed starting observations; best retained endpoints, last proposals and digest final_molecules are distinguished: the digest final excerpt is late seed-2 proposals, not all three final retained leaders. Actual generating-parent/emission/accepted joins are recorded for every leader below and fully retained in .slots/round-0026-slot-1/molecular_audit.json. Chronological delivery audit: child: 4350 accepted offspring; 682 strict best-parent beats and 269 logged incumbent-improvement flags during sequential accepted-feedback processing; among parent beats 667 had later actual generating-parent draws, 569 had accepted direct descendants, 15 had no later draw, and 13 occurred in the final batch; parent: 4350 accepted offspring; 629 strict best-parent beats and 258 logged incumbent-improvement flags during sequential accepted-feedback processing; among parent beats 614 had later actual generating-parent draws, 536 had accepted direct descendants, 15 had no later draw, and 12 occurred in the final batch. Later generating-parent draws include unsuccessful/unselected breeding, so they are not accepted-descendant counts; accepted direct descendants can overlap in ancestry, and terminal unused events are censored rather than failures. Incumbent-improvement flags are logged during sequential processing of each accepted batch and must not be mistaken for the preregistered batch pre-feedback incumbent statistic. All accepted offspring labels and joins came from existing trajectories/logs. Inherited gaps retain original source n-c55c3d520a2c, the same-code baseline n-62daf219c70a, and current source n-ea03f38e7e10 with their profile conditions; the full original policy-node molecular reports were read through the evidence index. No missing paths or absent matched comparisons were found.

per_task.generated_character: The three seed leaders have 24, 25 and 25 heavy atoms. They retain fused indole-like rings attached through an amide or N-hydroxy amide to phenyl/pyridyl rings. Seed 0 adds a partially unsaturated nitrogen ring and hydroxymethyl group while retaining an N-fluoro amide; seed 1 has a conventional secondary amide and N-fluoromethyl indole; seed 2 carries an aryl N-methyl-N-chloro group and N-hydroxy amide. The recognizable aromatic/carbonyl framework is medicinal-chemistry-like, but N-F/N-Cl environments make several leading examples questionable synthesis or stability targets. Published Parent leaders use a cumulene/azaaryl family, N-fluoroindole N-hydroxy amide, and N-chloroindole vicinal diketone respectively; the Child changes leading families without consistently resolving local reactive chemistry. The digest reads 870 optimizer proposals across seeds: ring-closure-string incidence 0.9908, aromatic-string incidence 0.9885, mean SMILES length 45.6, maximum 94, halogen-string incidence 0.9724. These are molecule-level SMILES text incidences, not ring counts or aromatic-atom fractions.
liabilities: N-fluoro amides and aryl N-methyl-N-chloro groups are distinct from conventional carbon-bound aromatic fluorine or chlorine and raise reactivity/stability concerns.

N-hydroxy amides are recognizable functionality but do not establish that the separate N-halogen bond is synthetically useful. Nearby leaders introduce N-O-F, N-Cl or more elaborate fused-ring substitutions.
missing_features: The high-scoring record does not consistently supply conventional nitrogen substitution while preserving the compact aromatic/amide arrangement; a conventional amide leader is present in one seed, so this is inconsistent coverage rather than inability to form amides.
Chemically independent plausible compact frameworks are limited among leaders within each seed. The trajectories cannot identify an exact absent target pharmacophore.
